column1: # The limits of the build that exist today: every place it states, in a rule or a refusal, that it builds for one platform only.
# Each is declared at its site by a `komira-limit:<id>` marker (a comment on the `target_compatible_with` line, or beside the
# refusal) and listed here with the PR that deletes it. //:limits (tools/build/platforms/limits) checks that the two agree:
#   - a `target_compatible_with` line with no marker, a marker with no row, and a row with no marker, are each refused;
#   - a row whose `retired_by` PR has merged (a commit subject on main contains `[native-pr:<n>]`) is refused, naming the
#     row: the platform table's check (test 37) reads git for it.
# `retired_by` is `native-pr:<n>` (the PR of the native-platform plan, tools/build/platforms/README.md) or `never`, which
# needs a reason that starts `product:`. Delete a row in the PR that deletes its marker. Columns are tab-separated.

column3: reason

third_party/aws-lc/BUCK: the cxx_library build of libcrypto, libssl and bssl, whose assembly lists are x86_64 ELF; on macOS arm64 :crypto is //src/awslc's archive instead, so :prefix_symbols and :crypto_symbols (the symbol checks of the x86_64 archive), libssl and bssl (the TLS interop peer) stay Linux-only

src/tests/conformance/komira_connect_conformance/BUCK, third_party/connect-conformance/BUCK: runs the connectconformance release pinned for linux-x86_64 only; it reaches darwin when s2n-tls does (8b), which then pins the release's darwin and linux aarch64 archives per platform

product: coverage is a property of the source, not of a platform: tools/build/toolchains/kcov/BUCK and the kcov_* pins of tools/build/platforms/table.bzl: line coverage of the sources is measured once, on linux-x86_64, by kcov (ptrace and ELF/DWARF), and tools/build/coverage/kcov/BUCK (cov_link, the link directory of a coverage build) and //:tests_greens (the coverage greens) exist there only; tools/build/toolchains/llvm_branch/BUCK and the llvm_branch_* pins: branch coverage's LLVM pieces exist on linux-x86_64 only; another platform's builds are not measured
tools/build/toolchains/defs.bzl: the C/C++ toolchain builds for linux-x86_64, and compiles and archives (links nothing) for macOS arm64; no other row has one
tools/build/run/BUCK: the macOS gate and its macOS unit test binaries are cross-built by the linux x86_64 zig, and those tests run only on macOS
tools/build/tests/functional/darwin/BUCK: tests host identity, which PR 12 deletes
tools/build/toolchains/darwin/BUCK: the macOS toolchain is its own package until the toolchains are row-driven and the package is deleted
tools/build/toolchains/darwin/BUCK: as darwin-mojo
tools/build/toolchains/darwin/BUCK: as darwin-mojo
tools/build/python_act/BUCK: the macOS build of python_act is cross-built by the linux x86_64 zig and runs only on macOS workers
third_party/python/BUCK: the macOS CPython is configured for darwin-arm64 only, so a linux graph query skips it and the macOS build of python_act it needs

product: tools/build/tests/functional/watchdog/BUCK: the process cases of the macOS compile wrapper (setsid, libproc, the host identity) run where that code runs, on a macOS worker; Linux has tests//functional/watchdog:cases

product: src/tests/helpers/komira_test_minio/BUCK: the probe's subject is the Linux kernel features (setpriv, PR_SET_PDEATHSIG, /proc) that the server end-to-end tests of komira's Linux server products need; another OS is probed by a test of its own, not by retiring this limit

third_party/git/BUCK, src/tests/conformance/komira_git_pack_conformance/BUCK, src/tests/conformance/komira_git_protocol_conformance/BUCK: the git oracle of git's conformance tests is built for linux-x86_64 first, and git-lfs is pinned as its amd64 release binary; the arm64 bring-up (14) adds the linux-arm64 build (zig cross-compiles git and curl; git-lfs publishes linux arm64)

src/tests/conformance/komira_http_conformance/BUCK: runs h2spec, whose release has amd64 builds only; it reaches darwin when s2n-tls does (8b), which then pins a darwin build or builds h2spec from source

product: OCI images, bundles and the launcher are Linux server products (tools/build/package/defs.bzl and oci_check.bzl: every macro is marked; tools/build/tests/functional/bundle_parity/BUCK); the table's `bundles` field says it per row

product: src/so/BUCK, tools/build/package/libkomira/BUCK and variants.bzl (the variants directories, their loads and the C driver, which uses glibc's link.h), python/tests/BUCK (variants_test, whose native directory holds the file VARIANTS beside the directory variants/, which a case-insensitive file system cannot hold): the per-CPU-level links of libkomira are the `isa_variants` of the linux-x86_64 row, x86-64 machine code that no other platform builds; another platform is skipped as incompatible

product: python/BUCK (dist_files), tools/build/package/libkomira/BUCK (dist_without_msupport), tools/build/package/libkomira/dist.bzl, elf_report.bzl, tools/build/package/install_check/install_check.bzl: the checks and negative fixtures of libkomira's Linux native directory read or load libkomira.so as ELF under glibc (dist_load.c is built for x86_64-linux-gnu.2.34 and asserts glibc's loader messages; so_report reads SONAME, RUNPATH, DT_NEEDED and GLIBC versions; the conda install check installs a linux-64 conda package and loads it with dlopen_probe and /proc/self/maps; the [dist] file names are .so); the macOS [dist] holds .dylib files read back by wheel_libs_macos_arm64, so another platform is skipped as incompatible

product: python/BUCK, python/install_test.bzl, tools/build/package/wheel.bzl, tools/build/package/BUCK: the manylinux linux-x86_64 wheel (//python:komira_wheel and the wheels derived from it), its read-backs (wheel_libs without a runtime directory), every test that installs one into the Linux interpreter, and the wheel rule's linux fixture (//tools/build/package:wheel_fixture and wheel_file_name_cases); they hold ELF libraries, and the wheel rule refuses a Mach-O member in a manylinux wheel, so another platform is skipped as incompatible; the macOS wheel is //python:komira_wheel_macos_arm64 (limit pypi-wheel-macos-arm64)
tools/build/toolchains/defs.bzl: no Mojo toolchain exists for a row that is not registered; arm64 gets one when it is brought up

product: ci/BUCK: //ci:pr and //ci:pr_default are the Linux part of the pull request check: they hold checks that exist on Linux only (the s2n probes of Linux features, OCI images, kcov coverage gates, the x86-64 ISA variants), each limited by its own row; macOS is built by the macOS step of pr / check, which builds //release:mopm_darwin_libs and never these (tools/build/ci/darwin.bzl)

tools/build/toolchains/defs.bzl: the protoc toolchain runs its tools on linux-x86_64 and serves linux-x86_64 and darwin-arm64 targets (what it writes is the same for both); another row gets it when that row is brought up

product: python/BUCK, python/smoke/BUCK, python/tests/BUCK: the macOS arm64 wheel, its install test, the pyarrow and protobuf wheels that test installs (and the macOS protobuf edge wheels of python/tests' 3.13 edge tests) and the smoke driver built for macOS are artifacts of the macos-arm64 release platform: configured for darwin-arm64 only, so a linux graph query skips them, and built by pypi.yml's macOS jobs alone, never by a pull request

product: tools/build/python/defs.bzl: a python_wheel, py_test or python_binding_test that names its interpreter as a plain label runs that interpreter, and every pinned one but third_party/python's cpython_macos (CPython 3.10, 3.11, 3.12, 3.13 for Linux, 3.14 and free-threaded 3.14) is a linux x86_64 python-build-standalone build whose wheels (the 3.14 closures, pyarrow for 3.11 and 3.12, the protobuf runtimes of those minors) are manylinux x86_64 files; those targets configure for linux-x86_64 only. The farm's macOS tests run CPython 3.13 alone, and the macOS wheel's other minors are installed and smoked on hosted macOS runners by pypi.yml

product: python/tests/BUCK (runtime_test): the subject is komira/_runtime.py's check of a Mojo runtime already loaded in the process, which exists on Linux only (a GNU build id read from an ELF file and dlinfo's origin; check_loaded_runtime does nothing off linux), and its stand-ins are ELF libraries (-Wl,-soname, --build-id=none) that only a Linux loader opens; another OS is skipped as incompatible

product: tools/build/readme_e2e/defs.bzl: the README e2e (//release/readme_e2e/verify, and //:readme_e2e_complete, which depends on it) tries the linux-64 files of a staged release as a user on the farm's Linux workers: the linux-64 .conda is unpacked, and the pinned mopm, the Mojo compiler and the gate run in a Linux action; the other platforms' files are held to the plan by hash and never unpacked (tools/build/readme_e2e/README.md, install); the macOS libraries are built and their welded tests run by //release:mopm_darwin_libs on the macOS workers, so another platform is skipped as incompatible

product: release/BUCK: //release:mopm_release_artifacts, the directory of both platforms the release publishes, configures its macOS half for darwin-arm64, which needs the macOS execution platform; it is compatible only under `-c komira_release.mac_tree=true`, passed where that platform is registered (release.yml's mopm-stage build, darwin_analysis.buckconfig), so a Linux graph query of `//...` skips it

product: release/release_set.bzl, tools/build/package/release_set.bzl: the release set and its check are the linux-64 .conda packages of a release (a .mojoc cannot be cross-compiled); osx-arm64 libraries are packed by mopm stage from //release:mopm_darwin_libs, so this set does not exist for another platform
tools/build/tests/run_tests.sh: the suite runs Linux x86_64 binaries and ELF tools on the client

tools/build/toolchains/defs.bzl: the Rust toolchain is the linux-x86_64 one; one per row. tools/build/rust/defs.bzl, third_party/rust/BUCK and tools/build/examples/rust/BUCK: every target the Rust rules make, and the crate list generated with it, is therefore linux-x86_64 only

product: tools/build/tests/functional/s2n_probes/defs.bzl: an s2n-tls feature probe compiles on the operating systems whose list in third_party/s2n-tls/features.bzl names it (clone, kTLS, Linux sendfile, glibc's features.h and cpuid.h on Linux only; minherit on macOS only), and its target is built for those

product: src/tests/helpers/komira_test_s3_adapter/BUCK, src/job_supervisor/BUCK (its two MinIO end-to-end binaries): the embedded MinIO's runner starts the server through setpriv with PR_SET_PDEATHSIG, the Linux kernel features the server end-to-end tests of komira's Linux server products use (as farm-probe-linux); another OS is skipped as incompatible

product: tools/build/selftest/defs.bzl: a self-test scenario drives buck2 from outside, so under an inner command of a scenario (-c komira_selftest.inner=true) every scenario is incompatible, and an inner //... skips them instead of running them a level deeper (the recursion guard, docs/design/build_selftests.md); no platform is excluded

product: tools/build/tests/functional/surface_capability_matrix/src/tests/e2e/pandas_e2e/BUCK: a planted macOS-only test that test 53 requires the surface capability matrix lint to refuse; a fixture of the check, not a platform limit
